title: Relations Overview
description: Understand 1-1, 1-N, and M-N relationships in Prisma, foreign key fields, and referential actions.

data.text: Relational databases derive their power from connections between tables. In Prisma, a relation connects two models. Relations are declared using the `@relation` attribute, which maps relation fields in Prisma to foreign key constraints in the database.
Relation Field vs Foreign Key Field

Prisma distinguishes between the **foreign key scalar field** (which physically exists as a column in the database) and the **relation field** (a virtual navigation property used in TypeScript queries that does NOT exist in the physical database table).

data.title: Foreign Key vs Relation Field Anatomy

rows: Deletes all connected child records automatically
Deleting a User deletes their Profile and Posts
Prevents deletion if child records exist (raises DB error)
Prevent deleting an Organization if active subscriptions exist
Sets the child's foreign key column to NULL
Deleting a Manager unassigns employees without deleting employees
PostgreSQL defers check until transaction commit
Circular foreign keys or deferred constraint validation

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Relation fields exist purely in Prisma and TypeScript; foreign key scalar fields exist in the database.
Always specify `onDelete: Cascade` or `Restrict` explicitly to define domain cleanup rules.
Prisma enforces referential actions at the database level when supported.
